To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the serum and liver-tissues levels of proinflammatory interleukine IL-6 were related to histology changes in the liver of patients with chronic HCV infection.

the serum levels of IL-4 and serum and liver tissue levels of IL-6 are higher in patients with chronic active hepatitis C than those with mild chronic persistent and moderate chronic active hepatitis C.
serum levels of IL-6 were significantly higher in patients with mild chronic active hepatitis compared with patients with moderate chronic persistent hepatitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in chronic hepatitis C.
the relationship between the proinflammatory cytokines and liver-tissue changes in HCV patients.
the levels of serum IL1-beta, IL-4, and IL-6 and the levels of IL-6 in liver tissue of HCV infected patients with chronic hepatitis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the levels of serum IL1beta, IL4, and IL6 in all HCV-infected subjects were higher compared with healthy controls, while the levels of liver tissue in all HCV-positive patients were higher compared to those in patients with liver cirrhotic disease without HBV or HC infection.
there was a significant correlation between the levels of serum IL1-beta and IL-4 and the levels of liver tissue cytokines.
the levels of serum IL1-beta, IL-4, and IL-6 are significantly higher in chronic HCV-infeceted patients when compared to healthy adults.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the levels of serum IL1beta and IL4 in patients with chronic hepatitis are higher than those of the healthy adults.
the levels of serum IL6 in patients with HCV infection were higher when compared with healthy adults.
the levels of IL-6 in serum and liver tissue are higher in patients with chronic HCV infection and the level of IL-6 is related to the histology changes of the liver.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proinflammatory cytokines play a major part in the pathogenesis of chronic HCV infection.
IL-1beta plays an important role in the progression of chronic hepatitis C, while IL-4 has no effect.
there is a positive correlation between the levels of IL-6 in serum and liver tissue in patients with HCV infection.
